svg.title: 3. Three kinds of data, three conflict rules
svg.text: Every write waits for a second Region to agree,
so write latency includes a cross-Region round trip.
pk = user#42, sk = pref#notify and sk = pref#language.
Two writers now touch two items, and both survive.
Result: no write conflicts, by design
The price: writes from us-west-2 are slower, and stop
until you fail over if us-east-1 is lost.
Active-active data: decide per table what "two Regions wrote at once" means
ledger table: DynamoDB global table, multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC)
• Exactly three Regions: three replicas, or two plus a witness.
• Every money movement is a conditional write on a version.
• Idempotency keys live here too, so a retry that lands in the
other Region still finds the first attempt.
• Keep the table small and hot: balances, holds, idempotency.
History goes to a cheaper store through streams.
• Check the MRSC feature list (for example transactions)
profiles table: DynamoDB global table, eventual consistency (MREC)
• Last writer wins is per item, so model data as small items
• Give each user a home Region claim in the token and send
their writes there while it is healthy.
• Append-only facts (devices, sessions) use unique sort keys
• Conditional writes only check the local replica: never use
this table to stop duplicate payments.
• Alarm on ReplicationLatency; it is your real RPO here.
KYC, merchants, settlement: Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database
• Apps connect through the global writer endpoint, so a
switchover or failover needs no config change.
• Planned move: switchover (RPO 0). Region loss: failover
with allow-data-loss, after a human decision.
• Watch AuroraGlobalDBRPOLag; Aurora PostgreSQL can cap it
• Keep it off the pay path. If it is read-only for five minutes,
